note: The speed ratchet's committed figures, read by `cargo xtask bench-check
--machine NAME` and held by `cargo xtask baseline` to the group files
`benches/<group>.rs` and their `[[bench]]` entries. Every figure under
`machines` is one criterion computed and wrote into its own
estimates.json on the machine it names; nothing re-times anything. See
docs/verification.md, 'Clocks: outside the suite, and not nowhere'.
`groups` lists each group's operations in the order its file declares
them. `unit` is pages, pixels, bytes, outlines or none; `per_iteration`
is how much of it one iteration processes, every call included; `calls`
is how many calls one iteration makes. An entry's `paired`, once set,
holds the `spread_percent` and the `band_percent` `bench-check --paired`
holds its median paired ratio to. A machine entry names in `unmeasured`
each listed operation it has no figure for yet.
`nanos` is the FASTEST mean of the stated runs, not their average: the
comparison is one-sided, faster is never a failure, so the bar worth
recording is the best the machine has ever done.
`swing_percent` is measured, never assumed, and every band is above its
own operation's swing. Key order is load-bearing -- `groups` comes before
`machines`, and the reader cuts each into entries at a first key: `group`
and then `name` in the lists, `machine` and then `id` in the machines,
where an entry's `unmeasured`, `cpu` and `held` come before its
`operations`.
A pinned machine's entry carries `cpu`, its host's /proc/cpuinfo model
name, and `held`, the frequency and core isolation it is held at, and
`bench-check` refuses to compare on a host whose model name is not `cpu`.
A fleet, such as `ubuntu-latest`, carries neither and compares on any
host.
